name: Crow Creek reservation for the Winnebago, Dakota Territory (1863), set apart under the Act of February 21, 1863
citation: Reservation created by executive order as authorized by the Act of February 21, 1863, 12 Stat. 658
promises: A reservation in present-day South Dakota for the Winnebago, created by executive order as authorized by the Act of February 21, 1863, which also directed the sale of their Minnesota reservation (Indian Claims Commission, Docket 243 findings).

breaches.what: The Winnebago claims, including compensation for the South Dakota reservation (Royce area 468) ceded by the treaty of March 8, 1865 and damages from the methods used to remove the tribe, were settled by a compromise final judgment of $4,600,000 in Dockets 243, 244 and 245.

compensation: A compromise final judgment of $4,600,000 in 1970 settled Dockets 243, 244 and 245, which covered several Winnebago cessions including Royce area 468; no part was assigned to this reservation alone.
today: By the treaty of March 8, 1865 (14 Stat. 671) the Winnebago ceded the South Dakota reservation and were given a reservation in northeast Nebraska on former Omaha land (Docket 243 findings).

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe says it was moved from northeast Iowa to Minnesota to South Dakota, that after the displacement to South Dakota many Winnebago travelled down the Missouri River under cover of darkness to rejoin relatives in Nebraska, and that its Nebraska reservation was established by treaties of 1865 and 1874.

openQuestions: This Royce record is the reservation set apart for the Winnebago at Crow Creek, not a cession; the tribe ceded it by the treaty of March 8, 1865, which has its own record.
The text of the Act of February 21, 1863 (12 Stat. 658) and of the order setting apart the reservation were not opened in this pass; the July 1, 1863 date is from treaties.json.

The Commission made no separate finding on Royce area 468 before the compromise. Secondary sources report heavy loss of life at Crow Creek between 1863 and 1865; no government admission or court finding on conditions there was located.
The Ho-Chunk Nation's own account of the removal was not found on its website.

plain.promised: Under an 1863 Act of Congress the Winnebago were removed from Minnesota to a new reservation at Crow Creek in present-day South Dakota.
plain.happened: The Winnebago Tribe of Nebraska says many people left Crow Creek by night down the Missouri River to reach relatives in Nebraska. The tribe gave up the reservation by an 1865 treaty. No finding of a broken promise was located.
plain.today: Claims covering this and other Winnebago land were settled for $4,600,000 in 1970 without a ruling on this reservation.
